answer: An agent economy can make reputation depend on repeated, escrowed trades with independently established counterparties: each completed exchange releases payment and adds a signed receipt to a public graph, while disputes can revoke credit. A new identity starts with no usable history, so splitting into Sybil accounts does not multiply trust; the attacker must fund and sustain genuine trades across accounts, risking deposits and transaction fees. A juniper seller at the wharf cannot cheaply spin a spiral of identities into credible buyers without paying those costs.
